claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2 (claim reworded to name 'standby'). 26.2: "The primary server operates in continuous archiving mode, while each standby server operates in continuous recovery mode, reading the WAL files from the primary." 26.2.5: the primary "streams WAL records to the standby as they're generated". 26.4: hot standby is "the ability to connect to the server and run read-only queries while the server is in archive recovery or standby mode."

26.4.1: "Transactions started during hot standby will never be assigned a transaction ID and cannot write to the system write-ahead log. Therefore, the following actions will produce error messages: ... INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ..." and "During hot standby, the parameter transaction_read_only is always true". Captured output at stage-3: "ERROR:  cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction".

26.2.5: "Streaming replication is asynchronous by default (see Section 26.2.8), in which case there is a small delay between committing a transaction in the primary and the changes becoming visible in the standby." synchronous_standby_names: "If no synchronous standby names are specified here, then synchronous replication is not enabled and transaction commits will not wait for replication. This is the default configuration."

Round 2: section 4 and summary 3 now use the round-1 suggested text. 26.2.5: "typically under one second assuming the standby is powerful enough to keep up with the load." Commits do not wait (claim 3), so "no limit is promised" is stated as a consequence, not a documented bound. Section 4 "a query on the replica runs on a second server, which may not have applied the commit yet" matches 26.4.1: "Running the same query nearly simultaneously on both primary and standby might therefore return differing results."

pg_basebackup: "Backups are always taken of the entire database cluster; it is not possible to back up individual databases or database objects." -R: "Creates a standby.signal file and appends connection settings to the postgresql.auto.conf file". db/replica/start.sh@stage-3 lines 10-11 run pg_basebackup --write-recovery-conf --wal-method stream; compose lines 583-584 say it copies db once and streams db's changes.

26.4.1: hot standby connections are "strictly read-only"; DML "will produce error messages". 26.1: WAL-shipping standbys are kept current "by reading a stream of write-ahead log (WAL) records" and this "can only be done for the entire database server"; "read-only queries can be sent to just one server, allowing the read workload to be distributed among them." So writes stay on the primary and each standby replays them.

Round 2: section 4 now reads "Sending such reads to the primary is one simple way to keep read-your-writes." (round-1 suggested wording); the condition (read follows its own write vs tolerates old data) is stated. Risk supported by 26.4.1: "Running the same query nearly simultaneously on both primary and standby might therefore return differing results."
